body.statement: Can the profiled-normal cross-fit handle be completed to construct \(\widehat\theta_U\) and \(\widehat\phi_U\), without observing \(b_n\), such that uniformly over every \(((P_n,b_n))\in\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_U-\theta(P_n))=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_n;b_n,P_0)(O_i)+o_{P_n}(1)\), \(\widehat V_U/V_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_n;b_n,P_0)\to_{P_n}1\), the conditional law of \(Z_n^{*}\) consistently estimates the corresponding studentized sampling law, and \(\inf_{((P_n,b_n))\in\mathfrak L_U(P_0)}P_n\{\theta(P_n)\in C_{n,1-\alpha}^{U}\}\to1-\alpha\), even when the active chart switches with \(n\)?
body.justification: This is the genuinely open step: estimating a profiled projection must remain stable along every root-\(n\) sequence in either branch, not merely at a fixed law.
body.gap: SunXieZhang2025, Theorem 4, proves branchwise multiplier consistency; NeweyRobins2018 controls cross-fit remainders for fixed smooth functionals; neither treats a score containing an estimated fixed-rank projection whose active identifying branch may switch locally.
body.consumer: A positive resolution gives one confidence interval for both the Alaska minimum-wage application and the sugary-drink-tax panels without pretesting which identifying branch holds.
